CARES Architecture Decision Package — Final Corrections

Status: Documentation-only architecture refinement. All schemas, SQL, pseudocode, cryptographic protocols, triggers, retention mechanisms, and worker behavior below are illustrative proposals—not production migrations, not implemented controls, and not verified behavior.

Status labels

  • EXISTING APPROVED REQUIREMENT — a mandatory CARES decision preserved by this review.
  • EXISTING PROPOSAL — a design already present in CARES architecture documents or prior gap analyses, not implemented.
  • NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION — a technical recommendation for owner, security, and engineering review.
  • OWNER DECISION REQUIRED — a commercial, privacy, legal, cryptographic, or security-owner decision not made here.
  • IMPLEMENTED AND TESTED — supported by working implementation and relevant tests.
  • NOT IMPLEMENTED — no working implementation exists.
  • NOT TESTED — no relevant PostgreSQL, cryptographic, integration, or security tests have been run.

1. Executive summary

Scope

This document resolves four remaining technical gaps identified during independent review of ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_PACKAGE_GAP_ANALYSIS_ROUND3.md:

  • Workstream A: trusted transaction context and GUC forgery.
  • Workstream B: expired-lease reclaimer, delivery-ambiguity recovery, and manual replay idempotency.
  • Workstream C: evidence metadata immutability, custody integrity, hash-chain limits, and purge/restore behavior.
  • Workstream D: PostgreSQL RLS interaction between UPDATE, SELECT, WHERE, RETURNING, and command-specific policies.

Findings

  • EXISTING APPROVED REQUIREMENT: Python backend, PostgreSQL primary database, external SaaS AI providers only, no local GPU requirement, one unique monitored device equals one licensed asset, multiple connectors reporting one device must not create duplicate licensed assets, and the original ten-phase roadmap remain unchanged.
  • NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Do not treat any custom PostgreSQL GUC as an authentication or authorization boundary. A GUC may carry only non-authoritative observability data. RLS helper functions must obtain verified context from a protected, verifier-written, transaction-bound record that runtime roles cannot forge or mutate.
  • NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: The verifier must be a hardened SECURITY DEFINER function with fixed search_path, minimal owner privileges, explicit EXECUTE grants, and no trust in caller-supplied tenant claims. It consumes the signed assertion nonce and records verified claims in a security-internal table bound to the current transaction and backend.
  • NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Add an explicit lease reclaimer protocol that fences prior lease tokens, records an expired attempt outcome, distinguishes “request not started”, “request started, outcome unknown”, and “request completed but acknowledgement lost” only where evidence supports that distinction, and defaults ambiguous external sends to delivery_unknown.
  • NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Make manual replay application idempotent with a unique replay-generation/application key and append-only replay records. attempt_count is cumulative and monotonic audit history, attempt_number is the unique sequence of an outbox attempt row, replay_generation is the authorization generation, and max_attempts applies per replay generation through an explicit generation-scoped counter. Authorized replay remains possible after a generation limit is reached and, for delivery_unknown, requires explicit reconciliation evidence and required authorization while enforcing duplicate_risk_accepted where applicable.
  • NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Treat core forensic_evidence identity, object, hash, provenance, and source fields as immutable after registration. Operational fields such as availability/legal-hold state may change only through controlled, audited procedures. Custody events are append-only. Database hash chains provide tamper evidence inside the database, not independent tamper-proof storage.
  • NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Do not assume UPDATE permission provides SELECT visibility. Row-addressed UPDATE ... WHERE ... RETURNING requires both UPDATE RLS qualification/checks and SELECT visibility/grants for columns/rows read by the command. Asset write scope should imply asset read scope for the same verified tenant and row set unless an approved alternative blind-write design is introduced.

Current status

  • NOT IMPLEMENTED: No trusted-context verifier, nonce registry, outbox worker, lease reclaimer, evidence registry, custody enforcement, RLS policies, or migrations exist.
  • NOT TESTED: No production-equivalent PostgreSQL role, RLS, transaction, replay, outbox, provider-reconciliation, evidence-immutability, or hash-chain tests have been run.
  • NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: The design is materially closer to formal PostgreSQL schema/security review for these four areas after privilege-chain, cleanup, immutability-enforcement, and outbox-replay corrections, but formal review must still select and validate the PostgreSQL version, transaction/binding mechanism, verifier implementation, role/grant model, provider reconciliation contracts, and retention/legal controls.

2. Workstream A — Trusted transaction context and GUC forgery

2.1 Why a custom GUC is not an authentication or authorization boundary

NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: A custom PostgreSQL GUC such as app.tenant_id, cares.verified_tenant_id, or cares.assertion is configuration state, not a cryptographic proof and not an authorization decision.

  • A GUC value can be present because a client set it, because pool middleware set it, because a previous transaction left state behind in a reused session, or because an attacker with SQL execution capability issued SET/set_config(...).
  • PostgreSQL evaluates RLS predicates using the current role/session/transaction state available to the query. If a policy reads current_setting('app.tenant_id', true) or similar, the policy is trusting mutable session state, not verifying a signed authorization.
  • A valid-looking tenant UUID in a GUC does not prove issuer, signature, audience, principal, scope, nonce freshness, or transaction binding.
  • RLS must fail closed. Therefore the source of truth for tenant and scope must be data that can only be created by an authorized verifier after successful assertion validation.

EXISTING PROPOSAL / ROUND 3 CONTEXT: Round 3 required security.context_is_valid(), security.current_verified_tenant_id(), and security.current_verified_scope_allows(...) and stated that verified context is transaction-local. This document refines that requirement by prohibiting GUC-backed authorization decisions.

2.2 GUC forgery and override paths

A runtime role or attacker with SQL execution in the same session could attempt:

Path Example Why it matters
Direct session set SET cares.tenant_id = 'tenant-b'; Changes session-visible configuration for later statements
Transaction-local set SELECT set_config('cares.tenant_id', 'tenant-b', true); Appears valid for the current transaction unless cleared
Function argument abuse Call a helper that accepts tenant/context arguments and stores them in GUCs Converts untrusted input into “context”
Pool/session bleed Reused session still contains old GUC value Wrong tenant appears selected after a missing reset
Nested function/trigger path Definer code calls set_config using attacker-influenced values Elevates untrusted state inside privileged execution
Search-path hijack before definer hardening Unqualified function resolves to attacker object Can redirect verification or context reads if definer/search path is unsafe

NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Runtime roles must not be granted permission to create or alter policies, roles, grants, or security functions. They must not be able to write security-internal verification tables. If custom GUCs are used for diagnostics, policies and authorization helpers must never read them for allow/deny decisions.

2.3 Viable designs for verified context storage

Design Description Strengths Risks / limits Recommendation
Protected transaction-bound record (preferred conceptual design) Verifier inserts a row in a security-internal table keyed to current backend and transaction after nonce consumption; helpers read that row for the current transaction only No trust in GUCs; auditable verifier boundary; can store verified claims and token hash/nonce reference; transaction rollback naturally discards nonce/claims only if designed in same transaction context Requires selected PostgreSQL transaction identifiers or equivalent binding strategy; helper reads add overhead; careful cleanup and backend/tx semantics required NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: preferred direction for formal review
Transaction-local temp table populated by definer verifier Verifier creates/populates pg_temp table with verified claims Naturally transaction/session scoped; easy conceptual lifetime Temp objects are accessible in-session; compromised runtime SQL in same session could tamper unless additional controls exist; not a strong boundary against same-session code execution Acceptable only if reviewed as same-session trusted code model; not preferred for untrusted-SQL resistance
Opaque context handle in GUC + protected lookup GUC stores random handle; actual claims live in protected table Avoids placing sensitive claims in GUC Still depends on not treating GUC as proof; handle theft/replay in same transaction/session must be bounded; adds complexity Viable only if helper validates handle against current backend/transaction and protected record; GUC remains non-authoritative
External verifier per statement Application/service asks external verifier for every query decision Separates crypto from DB High latency; difficult transaction atomicity; cannot replace DB RLS; failure modes complex Not recommended as primary RLS context source
Rely on GUC set by middleware Middleware sets tenant GUC before query Simple Not an authentication boundary; forgeable/misconfigurable; pool bleed risk Not acceptable for tenant isolation

2.4 Recommended trusted-context protocol

NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Use a protected verifier-written transaction context record.

BEGIN
  SELECT security.verify_and_bind_tenant_context(:signed_assertion);
    -> verify canonical claims, signature, issuer, audience, key status, principal,
       tenant, scopes, request/job, timestamps, lifetime, skew
    -> INSERT security.tenant_context_nonce (...) in same transaction
    -> INSERT security.verified_transaction_context (...) for current backend+transaction
    -> RETURN sanitized success (no full context record)

  -- business SQL; RLS/policies call narrow helpers that read protected current-transaction state
  INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE ...;

  SELECT security.clear_verified_transaction_context(); -- explicit transaction-end cleanup
COMMIT or ROLLBACK

Illustrative tables:

-- Security-internal schema: no runtime/worker grants.
REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA security FROM PUBLIC;

CREATE TABLE security.tenant_context_nonce (
    signing_key_id text NOT NULL,
    token_id uuid NOT NULL,
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    principal_id text NOT NULL,
    service_id text NOT NULL,
    request_or_job_id text NOT NULL,
    allowed_scope_digest bytea NOT NULL,
    issued_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    not_before timestamptz,
    expires_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    consumed_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp(),
    PRIMARY KEY (signing_key_id, token_id),
    CHECK (expires_at > issued_at),
    CHECK (expires_at <= issued_at + interval '60 seconds')
);

CREATE TABLE security.verified_transaction_context (
    backend_pid integer NOT NULL,
    transaction_ref text NOT NULL, -- implementation-selected stable current-tx binding
    binding_epoch text NOT NULL,  -- reviewed backend/session epoch or equivalent anti-reuse marker
    signing_key_id text NOT NULL,
    token_id uuid NOT NULL,
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    principal_id text NOT NULL,
    service_id text NOT NULL,
    actor_type text NOT NULL,
    request_or_job_id text NOT NULL,
    audience text NOT NULL,
    allowed_scopes text[] NOT NULL,
    verified_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    expires_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    bound_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp(),
    PRIMARY KEY (backend_pid, transaction_ref),
    FOREIGN KEY (signing_key_id, token_id)
        REFERENCES security.tenant_context_nonce (signing_key_id, token_id)
);

Implementation note (conceptual): transaction_ref must identify the current database transaction unambiguously for the backend and must be obtained by a reviewed mechanism selected with the PostgreSQL version. binding_epoch (or an equivalent reviewed guard) must prevent a stale row from being treated as valid after backend PID reuse or session recycling. This document does not assume a specific PostgreSQL major version, extension, or built-in transaction identifier function is available.

2.5 Nested execution, privileges, and narrowly scoped helpers

Nested execution (PostgreSQL): when an RLS policy or a SECURITY INVOKER function calls a SECURITY DEFINER function, PostgreSQL evaluates the definer function with the privileges of the function owner (not the calling role), while the call itself still requires EXECUTE privilege on that function. A SECURITY INVOKER wrapper therefore does not gain direct table privileges; it can only obtain what the definer function returns if EXECUTE is granted. This means RLS evaluation can succeed without granting runtime roles SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on security.verified_transaction_context or security.tenant_context_nonce.

NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Do not expose current_verified_context_row() or any function returning the complete verified context record to ordinary runtime or worker roles. Prefer narrow definer helpers that return only the required decision/value:

-- Narrow definer helper: reads protected row, returns no full record.
CREATE FUNCTION security.current_verified_tenant_id()
RETURNS uuid
LANGUAGE sql
STABLE
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = pg_catalog, security
AS $$
  SELECT c.tenant_id
  FROM security.verified_transaction_context c
  WHERE c.backend_pid = pg_backend_pid()
    AND c.transaction_ref = security.current_transaction_ref()
    AND c.binding_epoch = security.current_binding_epoch()
    AND c.expires_at + interval '30 seconds' >= clock_timestamp()
  LIMIT 1;
$$;

CREATE FUNCTION security.context_is_valid()
RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE sql
STABLE
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = pg_catalog, security
AS $$
  SELECT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM security.verified_transaction_context c
    WHERE c.backend_pid = pg_backend_pid()
      AND c.transaction_ref = security.current_transaction_ref()
      AND c.binding_epoch = security.current_binding_epoch()
      AND c.expires_at + interval '30 seconds' >= clock_timestamp()
  );
$$;

CREATE FUNCTION security.current_verified_scope_allows(required_scope text)
RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE sql
STABLE
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = pg_catalog, security
AS $$
  SELECT COALESCE(bool_or(required_scope = s.scope), false)
  FROM security.verified_transaction_context c
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL unnest(c.allowed_scopes) AS s(scope)
  WHERE c.backend_pid = pg_backend_pid()
    AND c.transaction_ref = security.current_transaction_ref()
    AND c.binding_epoch = security.current_binding_epoch()
    AND c.expires_at + interval '30 seconds' >= clock_timestamp();
$$;

SECURITY INVOKER wrappers with the same names/signatures may be used only if they add no privilege and are not required for exposure; direct narrow definer helpers in policies are acceptable if ownership, grants, and search paths are hardened and reviewed. A function that returns the full security.verified_transaction_context row, if needed for controlled diagnostics, must be owned/guarded separately and must not be executable by cares_runtime or cares_worker.

2.6 Ownership, privileges, search_path, and role boundaries for SECURITY DEFINER functions

Function Owner Execute grants Runtime/worker table access Required hardening
security.verify_and_bind_tenant_context(assertion) cares_security_owner (NOLOGIN) cares_runtime, cares_worker as required by call path; never PUBLIC No direct access to nonce/context tables SECURITY DEFINER, fixed search_path = pg_catalog, security, REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC, validates/consumes nonce, writes verified claims only, no unsafe dynamic SQL, sanitized audit/failure
security.clear_verified_transaction_context() cares_security_owner (NOLOGIN) cares_runtime, cares_worker as required; never PUBLIC No direct table grants SECURITY DEFINER, fixed search_path, deletes only current backend/transaction/binding row
security.current_verified_tenant_id() cares_security_owner (NOLOGIN) cares_runtime, cares_worker for RLS evaluation; never PUBLIC No direct table grants Narrow SECURITY DEFINER, fixed search_path, returns only uuid or NULL
security.context_is_valid() cares_security_owner (NOLOGIN) cares_runtime, cares_worker for RLS evaluation; never PUBLIC No direct table grants Narrow SECURITY DEFINER, fixed search_path, returns boolean only
security.current_verified_scope_allows(text) cares_security_owner (NOLOGIN) cares_runtime, cares_worker for RLS evaluation; never PUBLIC No direct table grants Narrow SECURITY DEFINER, fixed search_path, validates argument, returns boolean only
security.cleanup_verified_transaction_context() (maintenance) cares_security_owner (NOLOGIN) cares_security_maintenance only; never PUBLIC, runtime, or worker No runtime table grants SECURITY DEFINER, fixed search_path, deletes only provably stale/inactive rows per cleanup rules
Controlled evidence/custody procedures and mutation triggers (Workstream C) cares_security_owner or dedicated cares_evidence_owner (NOLOGIN) Narrow maintenance/evidence roles only where applicable; never PUBLIC, runtime, or worker unless explicitly required and reviewed No direct ad hoc evidence mutation for runtime/admin application roles SECURITY DEFINER only where required, fixed search_path, append-only custody enforcement, immutable-field enforcement, audited state transitions

Common requirements: owner is NOLOGIN with least privilege; schema/object ownership prevents earlier search-path shadowing; no unqualified object references; no dynamic SQL from untrusted input except reviewed whitelisted identifiers; REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION ... FROM PUBLIC; explicit grants only; runtime roles cannot ALTER, REPLACE, own, or grant these functions.

2.7 Transaction, pooling, cleanup, and reuse handling

  • Transaction binding: a verified context is valid only for the current backend transaction and binding epoch. Commit or rollback ends the authorization window. A new tenant transaction requires a newly verified assertion and fresh nonce consumption.
  • Explicit cleanup: clear_verified_transaction_context() must delete only the row matching the current backend PID, current transaction reference, and current binding epoch. It should run at controlled transaction completion before commit/rollback finalization where possible and be safe to call when no row exists.
  • Cleanup of committed records: committed rows must never authorize later transactions. Maintenance cleanup may remove rows only when they are provably not associated with an active transaction for that backend/binding context, or when they are older than the maximum assertion lifetime plus approved clock-skew/safety window and cannot match a current binding epoch. Cleanup must use a reviewed liveness/binding check; it must not delete by backend PID alone.
  • Backend PID reuse: PostgreSQL may reuse backend PIDs over time. backend_pid + transaction_ref is insufficient without a reviewed anti-reuse guard (binding_epoch or equivalent). A row from a previous backend/session epoch must compare unequal and fail closed.
  • Transaction identifier lifetime/reuse: transaction identifiers may be reused over time depending on PostgreSQL version and database activity. The selected transaction_ref mechanism must be transaction-current and combined with binding epoch/liveness rules so an old committed row cannot match a future transaction.
  • Abandoned connections: if a client disconnects or a transaction is abandoned, pool/proxy teardown or maintenance cleanup removes stale rows only after the backend/session is no longer active for that binding context. Until then, rows remain non-authorizing because helpers require the current backend/transaction/binding match.
  • Connection pooling: poolers must reset session state at check-in/check-out. Application code must not reuse a connection with an open transaction or uncleared temporary state. If reset/cleanup cannot be confirmed, the connection is discarded.
  • Rollback/unknown commit: rollback discards uncommitted nonce/context writes. Unknown commit outcomes require a fresh assertion and business idempotency; do not reuse the prior assertion.
  • Fail closed: missing, stale, expired, wrong-backend, wrong-transaction, wrong-epoch, or unverified context causes helper functions to return false/NULL, and restrictive RLS denies access.
  • GUC cleanup: observability GUCs, if any, are cleared on transaction end but are never used for authorization decisions.

2.8 Forged GUC prevention

A forged tenant GUC is prevented from changing verified context because:

  1. RLS helper functions do not read tenant/scope GUCs.
  2. Only security.verify_and_bind_tenant_context(...) can insert nonce/context rows, and it does so only after validating a signed assertion.
  3. Runtime/worker roles have no direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/SELECT privileges on security.tenant_context_nonce or security.verified_transaction_context.
  4. Narrow definer helpers derive tenant, validity, and scope from the protected current backend/transaction/binding record only.
  5. Committed or stale context rows cannot authorize a later transaction because helpers require a current transaction/binding match and cleanup/removal rules preserve fail-closed behavior.

2.9 Threat model and negative tests

Threat Expected outcome
Runtime role sets cares.tenant_id/app.tenant_id to another tenant No effect; RLS helpers ignore GUCs and deny or enforce verified tenant only
Runtime role inserts fake verified_transaction_context row Permission denied; table is security-internal
Runtime role calls verifier without valid signed assertion Verification fails; no context row; transaction denied
Attacker replays previously committed assertion in new transaction Nonce unique key rejects replay
Session reuse leaves stale GUC value Pool reset/deny-on-uncertain-cleanup required; stale GUC cannot authorize access
Attacker creates object earlier in search path for definer function Hardened fixed search_path and schema ownership prevent resolution
Attacker invokes definer function directly Execute privilege restricted; function still requires valid assertion or returns only current-transaction verified state
Compromised runtime SQL in same session tampers temp-table design Demonstrates why temp-table-only designs are weaker; protected security table is preferred

NOT TESTED: No GUC-forgery, pool-reuse, definer-hardening, or PostgreSQL transaction-binding tests exist.

3. Workstream B — Outbox expired-lease reclaimer and replay idempotency

3.1 Attempt and generation semantics

NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Define counters explicitly:

Field Meaning Monotonicity Notes
identity_operation_outbox.attempt_count Total attempts ever associated with the logical outbox message across all replay generations Monotonically increasing Cumulative audit count; never reset
identity_operation_outbox.generation_attempt_count Attempts consumed in the current replay generation Resets to 0 only by authorized replay application; otherwise increments on claim Compared to max_attempts for claim eligibility in the current generation
identity_operation_outbox.max_attempts Maximum claims/attempts allowed per replay generation Configuration value, not a counter Per-generation limit; reaching it does not prevent an authorized replay into a new generation
identity_operation_outbox.replay_generation Authorization generation for retries/replays after a terminal/manual disposition or explicit replay approval Increments only on authorized replay transition Binds outbox, attempt records, and replay application
identity_operation_outbox_attempt.attempt_number Unique sequence number of a specific attempt row for one outbox message Unique per (tenant_id, outbox_id); equals cumulative attempt_count at claim time Primary audit key for the attempt; never reused
identity_operation_outbox_attempt.replay_generation Replay generation under which that attempt ran Copied from outbox at claim time Prevents mixing attempts from different authorizations
identity_operation_outbox_attempt.generation_attempt_number Sequence of the attempt within its replay generation Unique per (tenant_id, outbox_id, replay_generation) Derived at claim as generation_attempt_count + 1; supports per-generation limit auditing
identity_operation_outbox_replay.target_replay_generation Generation that will become active when this replay is applied Unique per applied replay target Prevents concurrent duplicate replay application

This preserves append-only history. Manual replay does not delete or renumber prior attempts. Claim eligibility uses the per-generation counter (generation_attempt_count < max_attempts for the current generation) while attempt_count remains a cumulative, monotonic audit total.

3.2 Revised illustrative outbox schema

CREATE TABLE identity_operation_outbox (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    outbox_id uuid NOT NULL,
    operation_id uuid NOT NULL,
    destination_id text NOT NULL,
    message_type text NOT NULL,
    payload jsonb NOT NULL,
    request_idempotency_key text NOT NULL,
    provider_idempotency_ref text,
    state text NOT NULL CHECK (
        state IN ('pending', 'leased', 'retry_wait', 'delivered',
                  'delivery_unknown', 'dead_letter', 'cancelled')
    ),
    attempt_count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (attempt_count >= 0),
    generation_attempt_count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (generation_attempt_count >= 0),
    max_attempts integer NOT NULL CHECK (max_attempts > 0),
    replay_generation integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (replay_generation >= 0),
    CHECK (generation_attempt_count <= max_attempts),
    next_attempt_at timestamptz,
    lease_owner text,
    lease_token uuid,
    lease_until timestamptz,
    provider_request_phase text CHECK (
        provider_request_phase IN ('not_started', 'request_started', 'response_observed')
    ),
    provider_request_started_at timestamptz,
    provider_response_observed_at timestamptz,
    last_error_class text,
    last_error_code text,
    delivered_at timestamptz,
    provider_receipt_ref text,
    delivery_disposition text,
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, outbox_id),
    UNIQUE (tenant_id, request_idempotency_key),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, operation_id)
        REFERENCES asset_identity_operation (tenant_id, operation_id),
    CHECK (
        (state = 'leased' AND lease_owner IS NOT NULL
                          AND lease_token IS NOT NULL
                          AND lease_until IS NOT NULL)
        OR
        (state <> 'leased' AND lease_owner IS NULL
                           AND lease_token IS NULL
                           AND lease_until IS NULL)
    )
);

CREATE TABLE identity_operation_outbox_attempt (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    outbox_id uuid NOT NULL,
    attempt_number integer NOT NULL CHECK (attempt_number > 0),
    replay_generation integer NOT NULL CHECK (replay_generation >= 0),
    generation_attempt_number integer NOT NULL CHECK (generation_attempt_number > 0),
    worker_id text NOT NULL,
    lease_token uuid NOT NULL,
    lease_claimed_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    lease_until timestamptz NOT NULL,
    provider_request_phase text NOT NULL CHECK (
        provider_request_phase IN ('not_started', 'request_started', 'response_observed')
    ),
    provider_request_started_at timestamptz,
    provider_response_observed_at timestamptz,
    completed_at timestamptz,
    outcome text CHECK (
        outcome IN ('delivered', 'retryable_failure', 'permanent_failure',
                    'delivery_unknown', 'lease_expired_before_request',
                    'lease_expired_after_request_start', 'cancelled')
    ),
    error_class text,
    error_code text,
    provider_request_ref text,
    provider_response_ref text,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, outbox_id, attempt_number),
    UNIQUE (tenant_id, outbox_id, replay_generation, generation_attempt_number),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, outbox_id)
        REFERENCES identity_operation_outbox (tenant_id, outbox_id)
);

CREATE TABLE identity_operation_outbox_replay (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    replay_id uuid NOT NULL,
    outbox_id uuid NOT NULL,
    target_replay_generation integer NOT NULL CHECK (target_replay_generation > 0),
    requested_by text NOT NULL,
    approved_by text,
    reason text NOT NULL,
    ticket_ref text NOT NULL,
    authorization_ref text NOT NULL,
    requested_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    approved_at timestamptz,
    applied_at timestamptz,
    state text NOT NULL CHECK (
        state IN ('requested', 'approved', 'rejected', 'applied', 'superseded')
    ),
    duplicate_risk_accepted boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    reconciliation_evidence_ref text,
    reconciliation_recorded_at timestamptz,
    provider_outcome text CHECK (provider_outcome IN ('unknown', 'not_delivered', 'delivered', 'not_applicable')),
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, replay_id),
    UNIQUE (tenant_id, outbox_id, target_replay_generation),
    CHECK (
        state <> 'applied'
        OR provider_outcome IS NOT NULL
    ),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, outbox_id)
        REFERENCES identity_operation_outbox (tenant_id, outbox_id)
);

3.3 Claim and request-phase marking

claim transaction:
  select eligible outbox row FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
    where state IN ('pending','retry_wait')
      and (next_attempt_at IS NULL OR next_attempt_at <= clock_timestamp())
      and generation_attempt_count < max_attempts
  if none: return
  next_attempt_number := outbox.attempt_count + 1
  next_generation_attempt_number := outbox.generation_attempt_count + 1
  update outbox:
    state='leased', lease_owner, lease_token, lease_until,
    attempt_count=next_attempt_number,
    generation_attempt_count=next_generation_attempt_number,
    replay_generation unchanged,
    provider_request_phase='not_started',
    provider_request_started_at=NULL, provider_response_observed_at=NULL
  insert attempt row with attempt_number, replay_generation,
    generation_attempt_number, lease_token

before external call transaction:
  update outbox and open attempt
    set provider_request_phase='request_started',
        provider_request_started_at=clock_timestamp()
  where current lease token still valid

external call:
  perform outside DB transaction
  if any response or provider-side receipt is observed, persist response_observed evidence
  in a fenced acknowledgement/reconciliation transaction

ack/reconcile transaction:
  update only if state='leased' and lease_token matches and lease valid as required

The request_started marker is critical: it does not prove provider completion, but it proves CARES crossed the boundary where duplicate external effects may be possible.

3.4 Expired-lease reclaimer pseudocode

reclaimer transaction (one outbox row):
  SELECT ... FROM identity_operation_outbox
  WHERE tenant_id = :tenant
    AND outbox_id = :outbox
    AND state = 'leased'
    AND lease_until <= clock_timestamp()
  FOR UPDATE;

  if not found: return no_op;

  capture prior_lease_token, prior_worker, prior_attempt_number,
          provider_request_phase, provider_idempotency_ref;

  -- Fence stale worker by clearing/replacing lease state in the same update.
  UPDATE identity_operation_outbox_attempt
  SET completed_at = clock_timestamp(),
      outcome = CASE
        WHEN provider_request_phase = 'not_started' THEN 'lease_expired_before_request'
        ELSE 'lease_expired_after_request_start'
      END,
      error_class = 'lease_expired'
  WHERE tenant_id=:tenant AND outbox_id=:outbox
    AND attempt_number=prior_attempt_number
    AND lease_token=prior_lease_token
    AND completed_at IS NULL;

  IF provider_request_phase = 'not_started' THEN
     UPDATE identity_operation_outbox
     SET state = CASE WHEN generation_attempt_count < max_attempts THEN 'retry_wait' ELSE 'dead_letter' END,
         next_attempt_at = CASE WHEN generation_attempt_count < max_attempts THEN clock_timestamp() + :retry_delay ELSE NULL END,
         lease_owner=NULL, lease_token=NULL, lease_until=NULL,
         last_error_class='lease_expired', last_error_code='before_request',
         updated_at=clock_timestamp()
     WHERE tenant_id=:tenant AND outbox_id=:outbox
       AND state='leased' AND lease_token=prior_lease_token;

  ELSIF provider has reliable idempotency for provider_idempotency_ref THEN
     UPDATE identity_operation_outbox
     SET state = CASE WHEN generation_attempt_count < max_attempts THEN 'retry_wait' ELSE 'delivery_unknown' END,
         next_attempt_at = CASE WHEN generation_attempt_count < max_attempts THEN clock_timestamp() + :retry_delay ELSE NULL END,
         lease_owner=NULL, lease_token=NULL, lease_until=NULL,
         last_error_class='lease_expired',
         last_error_code='after_request_start_idempotent',
         updated_at=clock_timestamp()
     WHERE tenant_id=:tenant AND outbox_id=:outbox
       AND state='leased' AND lease_token=prior_lease_token;

  ELSE
     UPDATE identity_operation_outbox
     SET state='delivery_unknown',
         next_attempt_at=NULL,
         lease_owner=NULL, lease_token=NULL, lease_until=NULL,
         delivery_disposition='manual_reconciliation_required',
         last_error_class='lease_expired',
         last_error_code='after_request_start_non_idempotent_or_unknown',
         updated_at=clock_timestamp()
     WHERE tenant_id=:tenant AND outbox_id=:outbox
       AND state='leased' AND lease_token=prior_lease_token;
  END IF;

The stale worker cannot later acknowledge delivery because acknowledgement requires state='leased' AND lease_token=:my_token; reclaiming has replaced/cleared that token.

3.5 Distinguishing crash timing and handling delivery_unknown

Evidence Classification Allowed transition
No request_started marker and no provider evidence Crashed or stopped before external send retry_wait/pending or dead_letter by attempt policy
request_started marker exists, provider supports idempotency, and idempotency key/reference is retained and valid Possibly sent, duplicate-safe retry path may exist retry_wait with same logical provider idempotency reference, or reconcile with evidence
request_started marker exists but provider has no reliable idempotency/reconciliation External effect may or may not have happened delivery_unknown
Provider receipt/lookup confirms success Delivery completed delivered with recorded reconciliation evidence
Provider receipt/lookup confirms no effect No delivery confirmed retry_wait only after explicit reconciliation evidence and required authorization

NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: delivery_unknown is a safety state, not a failure to be auto-cleared. Transition from delivery_unknown to retry_wait requires explicit reconciliation evidence (reconciliation_evidence_ref/record, provider outcome, actor, time) and the required authorization. For ambiguous/non-idempotent cases where duplicate external effects remain possible, replay application must also record and enforce duplicate_risk_accepted=true; storing the field without enforcement is insufficient. Do not claim exactly-once external delivery.

3.6 Manual replay idempotency

NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Replay application must be atomic and unique:

-- illustrative pseudocode in one transaction
SELECT state, replay_generation, attempt_count, generation_attempt_count,
       provider_idempotency_ref, delivery_disposition
FROM identity_operation_outbox
WHERE tenant_id=:tenant AND outbox_id=:outbox
FOR UPDATE;

-- require approved replay row for next generation
SELECT *
FROM identity_operation_outbox_replay
WHERE tenant_id=:tenant AND replay_id=:replay_id
  AND outbox_id=:outbox
  AND state='approved'
  AND target_replay_generation = :current_replay_generation + 1
FOR UPDATE;

-- if not found: reject duplicate/concurrent/stale replay
-- if outbox.state = 'delivery_unknown':
--   require replay.reconciliation_evidence_ref IS NOT NULL
--   require replay.reconciliation_recorded_at IS NOT NULL
--   require replay.provider_outcome IS NOT NULL
--   if provider outcome/effect remains ambiguous or non-idempotent duplicate risk exists:
--     require replay.duplicate_risk_accepted = true
-- if outbox.state NOT IN ('dead_letter','delivery_unknown','retry_wait' by approved policy): reject

UPDATE identity_operation_outbox_replay
SET state='applied', applied_at=clock_timestamp()
WHERE tenant_id=:tenant AND replay_id=:replay_id
  AND outbox_id=:outbox
  AND state='approved'
  AND target_replay_generation = :current_replay_generation + 1;

-- if rowcount != 1 then reject duplicate/concurrent/stale replay

UPDATE identity_operation_outbox
SET replay_generation = replay_generation + 1,
    generation_attempt_count = 0,  -- resets per-generation limit only; attempt_count remains cumulative
    state = 'retry_wait',
    next_attempt_at = clock_timestamp(),
    delivery_disposition = NULL,
    last_error_class = NULL,
    last_error_code = NULL,
    updated_at = clock_timestamp()
WHERE tenant_id=:tenant AND outbox_id=:outbox;
-- preserve request_idempotency_key and provider_idempotency_ref

Controls:

  • UNIQUE (tenant_id, outbox_id, target_replay_generation) prevents two applied replay records for the same generation.
  • The apply transaction locks the outbox row, verifies current generation, marks the replay applied, and increments generation exactly once.
  • A second concurrent request sees no approved replay at the expected generation or loses the row lock race; it must return the existing replay/result, not apply again.
  • Manual replay preserves request_idempotency_key and provider_idempotency_ref; a new external idempotency key/reference is allowed only if a separately approved new logical side effect is explicitly created and recorded with authorization and duplicate-risk acceptance. Reusing the original provider idempotency reference is the default.
  • delivery_unknown replay requires explicit reconciliation evidence, provider outcome, and required authorization before transition to retry_wait. Where duplicate external effects remain possible, duplicate_risk_accepted=true is mandatory and enforced by the apply procedure/constraints, not merely stored.
  • Authorized replay after a per-generation limit is reached increments replay_generation, resets only generation_attempt_count, preserves cumulative attempt_count, and appends a new attempt history when claimed.

3.7 Outbox state transitions

Current Event Next Conditions
pending Claim + attempt insert leased FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, generation_attempt_count < max_attempts, new lease token, cumulative attempt_number, generation attempt number
retry_wait Due claim leased Same as pending; per-generation limit applies
leased Provider success confirmed delivered Current lease token matches; receipt recorded
leased Retryable failure observed retry_wait Bounded per-generation retry policy allows
leased Permanent failure observed dead_letter Sanitized error recorded
leased Lease expired, no request started retry_wait or dead_letter Attempt marked lease_expired_before_request; uses per-generation counter
leased Lease expired, request started, idempotent retry allowed retry_wait or delivery_unknown Preserve same provider idempotency reference
leased Lease expired, request started, ambiguous/non-idempotent delivery_unknown Manual reconciliation required
delivery_unknown Provider lookup confirms delivered delivered Explicit reconciliation evidence recorded
delivery_unknown Provider lookup confirms not delivered retry_wait Explicit reconciliation evidence and required authorization recorded
dead_letter Authorized replay applied retry_wait New replay generation, generation_attempt_count reset, cumulative attempt_count preserved
delivery_unknown Authorized replay applied retry_wait or remain blocked Explicit reconciliation evidence, required authorization, and enforced duplicate_risk_accepted where applicable
nonterminal Explicit cancellation before external effect cancelled Cancellation audited; no history erased

NOT IMPLEMENTED / NOT TESTED: No worker, reclaimer, provider adapters, or replay authorization workflow exists.

4. Workstream C — Evidence metadata immutability and custody integrity

4.1 Immutable versus operationally mutable fields

NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Separate immutable evidence facts from controlled operational state. The immutable-field inventory below is authoritative for the illustrative trigger/procedure design; any schema change must update both the inventory and enforcement.

Immutable forensic_evidence fields (no direct UPDATE/DELETE; correction requires a new evidence record and append-only custody/lineage references):

Field Nullability (illustrative) Enforcement note
tenant_id NOT NULL Tenant identity is immutable
evidence_id NOT NULL Evidence identity is immutable
evidence_store_id NOT NULL Registered store binding is immutable
object_key NOT NULL Immutable object identity within store
object_version_id NOT NULL Immutable object version identity
hash_algorithm NOT NULL Digest algorithm used at registration
content_hash NOT NULL Registration digest
content_length NOT NULL Registration byte length
media_type NULL allowed Use IS DISTINCT FROM in trigger
source_kind NOT NULL Source classification immutable
source_data_source_id NULL allowed Use IS DISTINCT FROM; pair consistency remains enforced
source_device_key_id NULL allowed Use IS DISTINCT FROM; pair consistency remains enforced
captured_at NULL allowed Use IS DISTINCT FROM
ingested_at NOT NULL Registration time immutable
collector_identity NOT NULL Collector identity immutable
provenance NOT NULL Original provenance payload immutable
created_at NOT NULL Record creation time immutable

Operationally mutable/controlled fields (no direct ad hoc updates):

Field Classification Allowed change after registration
retention_policy_id Controlled metadata May change only through security.set_evidence_retention_policy(...) or equivalent controlled procedure with authorization, validation, and append-only custody event
legal_hold Operationally mutable May change only through security.set_evidence_legal_hold(...) with authorization and append-only custody event
availability_state Operationally mutable May change only through controlled procedures: security.request_evidence_purge(...), security.complete_evidence_purge(...), security.cancel_evidence_purge(...), security.mark_evidence_integrity_failed(...), security.revalidate_evidence(...), each enforcing allowed transitions and append-only custody events
Custody hash-chain state stored on custody-event rows Immutable append-only history Never rewritten; chain linkage is maintained only by append procedure

4.2 Permissions, restrictions, and controlled procedures

-- Illustrative privilege intent
REVOKE ALL ON forensic_evidence FROM PUBLIC, cares_runtime, cares_worker;
REVOKE ALL ON evidence_custody_event FROM PUBLIC, cares_runtime, cares_worker;
REVOKE ALL ON TABLE security.evidence_transition_authorization FROM PUBLIC,
    cares_runtime, cares_worker, cares_evidence_ingest, cares_evidence_reader, cares_evidence_admin;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON forensic_evidence TO cares_evidence_ingest;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON evidence_custody_event TO cares_evidence_ingest;
GRANT SELECT ON forensic_evidence, evidence_custody_event TO cares_evidence_reader;

-- No direct UPDATE/DELETE on forensic_evidence or evidence_custody_event for ordinary
-- runtime, worker, or administrative application roles. Controlled procedures only.
REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON forensic_evidence FROM cares_evidence_ingest, cares_evidence_reader, cares_evidence_admin;
REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON evidence_custody_event FROM cares_evidence_ingest, cares_evidence_reader, cares_evidence_admin;

-- security.evidence_transition_authorization is security-internal: only security/evidence-owner
-- definer code may access it. Ordinary runtime, worker, ingest, reader, and administrative
-- application roles have no privileges.

NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Replace the GUC-based controlled-transition guard with a protected transaction-bound authorization mechanism. A PostgreSQL custom GUC (including security.evidence_controlled_transition) is session configuration state and is not proof that an authorized SECURITY DEFINER procedure initiated the transition; runtime sessions may be able to set it via SET/set_config(). Do not use any custom GUC as an authorization source. GUCs may be used only for non-authoritative diagnostics and must never be read by triggers, RLS policies, or authorization helpers for allow/deny decisions.

Use hardened SECURITY DEFINER procedures for legal-hold changes, retention metadata changes, purge state transitions, integrity-failure marking, and revalidation. Each procedure must: authenticate and authorize the requested transition under a valid protected transaction context (Workstream A narrow helpers), validate preconditions against the target evidence row, create a security-internal transaction-bound authorization, perform exactly one controlled UPDATE, append the required custody event, and verify single-use consumption — all in the same database transaction. Triggers must reject direct updates to immutable columns, reject all deletes, and reject controlled-field changes unless an exact, unconsumed, current-transaction authorization exists and is consumed atomically for that tenant, evidence record, and permitted operation/transition.

Protected transaction-bound authorization (reuses Workstream A binding helpers):

CREATE TABLE security.evidence_transition_authorization (
    authorization_id uuid NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    backend_pid integer NOT NULL,
    transaction_ref text NOT NULL,
    binding_epoch text NOT NULL,
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    evidence_id uuid NOT NULL,
    operation_key text NOT NULL CHECK (
        operation_key IN (
            'set_legal_hold',
            'set_retention_policy',
            'request_evidence_purge',
            'complete_evidence_purge',
            'cancel_evidence_purge',
            'mark_evidence_integrity_failed',
            'revalidate_evidence'
        )
    ),
    expected_old_legal_hold boolean,
    expected_new_legal_hold boolean,
    expected_old_retention_policy_id uuid,
    expected_new_retention_policy_id uuid,
    expected_old_availability_state text,
    expected_new_availability_state text,
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp(),
    consumed_at timestamptz,
    consumed_by_update boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    CHECK (consumed_at IS NULL OR consumed_by_update = true),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, evidence_id)
        REFERENCES forensic_evidence (tenant_id, evidence_id)
);

-- At most one pending authorization per current transaction/binding/evidence/operation.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX evidence_transition_authorization_pending_uq
    ON security.evidence_transition_authorization (
        backend_pid, transaction_ref, binding_epoch, tenant_id, evidence_id, operation_key
    )
    WHERE consumed_at IS NULL;

REVOKE ALL ON security.evidence_transition_authorization FROM PUBLIC,
    cares_runtime, cares_worker, cares_evidence_ingest, cares_evidence_reader, cares_evidence_admin;

Illustrative controlled procedure, helper, and trigger intent:

-- Controlled SECURITY DEFINER procedure: only this authorized path may create authorization.
CREATE FUNCTION security.set_evidence_legal_hold(
    p_tenant_id uuid,
    p_evidence_id uuid,
    p_new_legal_hold boolean,
    p_request_or_job_id text
)
RETURNS void
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = pg_catalog, security
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_old_legal_hold boolean;
  v_old_availability text;
  v_old_retention uuid;
  v_auth_id uuid := gen_random_uuid();
  v_consumed boolean;
BEGIN
  -- 1) Authenticate/authorize under protected transaction context.
  IF NOT security.context_is_valid()
     OR security.current_verified_tenant_id() IS DISTINCT FROM p_tenant_id
     OR NOT security.current_verified_scope_allows('evidence:controlled_transition') THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'verified context or scope missing';
  END IF;

  -- 2) Lock target evidence row and validate requested transition/preconditions.
  SELECT legal_hold, availability_state, retention_policy_id
    INTO v_old_legal_hold, v_old_availability, v_old_retention
  FROM forensic_evidence
  WHERE tenant_id = p_tenant_id AND evidence_id = p_evidence_id
  FOR UPDATE;

  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'evidence not found';
  END IF;
  IF v_old_legal_hold IS NOT DISTINCT FROM p_new_legal_hold THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'no-op transition not authorized';
  END IF;
  -- Additional authorization/precondition checks (actor, policy, retention/legal constraints) required.

  -- 3) Create security-internal authorization bound to current tx/binding/tenant/evidence/operation.
  INSERT INTO security.evidence_transition_authorization (
      authorization_id, backend_pid, transaction_ref, binding_epoch,
      tenant_id, evidence_id, operation_key,
      expected_old_legal_hold, expected_new_legal_hold,
      expected_old_retention_policy_id, expected_new_retention_policy_id,
      expected_old_availability_state, expected_new_availability_state
  ) VALUES (
      v_auth_id, pg_backend_pid(), security.current_transaction_ref(), security.current_binding_epoch(),
      p_tenant_id, p_evidence_id, 'set_legal_hold',
      v_old_legal_hold, p_new_legal_hold,
      v_old_retention, v_old_retention,
      v_old_availability, v_old_availability
  );

  -- 4) Exactly one controlled update; trigger verifies and atomically consumes authorization.
  UPDATE forensic_evidence
     SET legal_hold = p_new_legal_hold
   WHERE tenant_id = p_tenant_id AND evidence_id = p_evidence_id;

  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'controlled evidence update failed';
  END IF;

  -- 5) Append required custody event in the same transaction (section 4.3 protocol).
  PERFORM security.append_evidence_custody_event(
      p_tenant_id, p_evidence_id, 'set_legal_hold', p_request_or_job_id,
      jsonb_build_object('old_legal_hold', v_old_legal_hold, 'new_legal_hold', p_new_legal_hold)
  );

  -- 6) Confirm single-use consumption. Rollback leaves no reusable authorization.
  SELECT (consumed_at IS NOT NULL AND consumed_by_update = true)
    INTO v_consumed
  FROM security.evidence_transition_authorization
  WHERE authorization_id = v_auth_id;

  IF NOT COALESCE(v_consumed, false) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'evidence transition authorization was not consumed';
  END IF;
END;
$$;

CREATE FUNCTION security.prevent_forensic_evidence_mutation()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = pg_catalog, security
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_operation_key text;
  v_auth_id uuid;
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'forensic_evidence rows are immutable; use controlled purge workflow';
  END IF;

  -- Immutable fields: null-safe comparisons required (authoritative inventory in section 4.1).
  IF NEW.tenant_id IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.tenant_id
     OR NEW.evidence_id IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.evidence_id
     OR NEW.evidence_store_id IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.evidence_store_id
     OR NEW.object_key IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.object_key
     OR NEW.object_version_id IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.object_version_id
     OR NEW.hash_algorithm IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.hash_algorithm
     OR NEW.content_hash IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.content_hash
     OR NEW.content_length IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.content_length
     OR NEW.media_type IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.media_type
     OR NEW.source_kind IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.source_kind
     OR NEW.source_data_source_id IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.source_data_source_id
     OR NEW.source_device_key_id IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.source_device_key_id
     OR NEW.captured_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.captured_at
     OR NEW.ingested_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.ingested_at
     OR NEW.collector_identity IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.collector_identity
     OR NEW.provenance IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.provenance
     OR NEW.created_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.created_at
  THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'immutable forensic_evidence fields cannot be changed';
  END IF;

  -- Controlled fields require exact, unconsumed, transaction-bound authorization.
  IF NEW.retention_policy_id IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.retention_policy_id
     OR NEW.legal_hold IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.legal_hold
     OR NEW.availability_state IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.availability_state
  THEN
    -- Derive permitted operation from the actual delta; reject unsupported combinations.
    IF NEW.legal_hold IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.legal_hold
       AND NEW.retention_policy_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.retention_policy_id
       AND NEW.availability_state IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.availability_state THEN
      v_operation_key := 'set_legal_hold';
    ELSIF NEW.retention_policy_id IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.retention_policy_id
       AND NEW.legal_hold IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.legal_hold
       AND NEW.availability_state IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.availability_state THEN
      v_operation_key := 'set_retention_policy';
    ELSIF NEW.availability_state IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.availability_state
       AND NEW.legal_hold IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.legal_hold
       AND NEW.retention_policy_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.retention_policy_id THEN
      v_operation_key := CASE
        WHEN OLD.availability_state = 'available' AND NEW.availability_state = 'purge_pending' THEN 'request_evidence_purge'
        WHEN OLD.availability_state = 'purge_pending' AND NEW.availability_state = 'purged' THEN 'complete_evidence_purge'
        WHEN OLD.availability_state = 'purge_pending' AND NEW.availability_state = 'available' THEN 'cancel_evidence_purge'
        WHEN OLD.availability_state = 'available' AND NEW.availability_state = 'integrity_failed' THEN 'mark_evidence_integrity_failed'
        WHEN OLD.availability_state = 'integrity_failed' AND NEW.availability_state = 'available' THEN 'revalidate_evidence'
        ELSE NULL
      END;
    ELSE
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'unsupported controlled evidence field combination';
    END IF;

    IF v_operation_key IS NULL THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'disallowed evidence transition';
    END IF;

    -- Atomically consume exactly one matching authorization for this current
    -- transaction/binding, tenant, evidence record, and permitted operation/transition.
    -- Authorizations from another transaction, backend/binding context, tenant, evidence
    -- record, or expired/invalid verified context cannot match; consumed authorizations
    -- cannot be reused. No generic bypass flag exists.
    WITH consumed AS (
      UPDATE security.evidence_transition_authorization a
         SET consumed_at = clock_timestamp(),
             consumed_by_update = true
       WHERE a.backend_pid = pg_backend_pid()
         AND a.transaction_ref = security.current_transaction_ref()
         AND a.binding_epoch = security.current_binding_epoch()
         AND a.tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id
         AND a.evidence_id = OLD.evidence_id
         AND a.operation_key = v_operation_key
         AND a.consumed_at IS NULL
         AND a.expected_old_legal_hold IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.legal_hold
         AND a.expected_new_legal_hold IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NEW.legal_hold
         AND a.expected_old_retention_policy_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.retention_policy_id
         AND a.expected_new_retention_policy_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NEW.retention_policy_id
         AND a.expected_old_availability_state IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.availability_state
         AND a.expected_new_availability_state IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NEW.availability_state
         AND security.context_is_valid()
         AND security.current_verified_tenant_id() IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.tenant_id
       RETURNING a.authorization_id
    )
    SELECT authorization_id INTO v_auth_id FROM consumed;

    IF v_auth_id IS NULL THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'controlled evidence update requires authorized transaction-bound transition';
    END IF;

    -- Defense-in-depth: allowed availability transitions only.
    IF NOT (
      (OLD.availability_state = 'available' AND NEW.availability_state IN ('purge_pending', 'integrity_failed'))
      OR (OLD.availability_state = 'purge_pending' AND NEW.availability_state IN ('purged', 'available'))
      OR (OLD.availability_state = 'integrity_failed' AND NEW.availability_state = 'available')
      OR OLD.availability_state IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NEW.availability_state
    ) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'disallowed evidence availability transition';
    END IF;
  END IF;

  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

Authorization and atomicity requirements (illustrative):

  • No GUC authorization: SET/set_config of security.evidence_controlled_transition or any other GUC cannot authorize a controlled evidence update. GUCs may carry only non-authoritative diagnostics if explicitly approved and are ignored by trigger/procedure authorization decisions.
  • Procedure responsibilities: controlled SECURITY DEFINER procedures authenticate and authorize the request, bind authorization to current transaction (backend_pid, transaction_ref, binding_epoch), tenant_id, evidence_id, and permitted operation_key/transition values, insert the authorization in the security-internal table, perform exactly one controlled UPDATE, append the required custody event, and verify consumption in the same transaction.
  • Trigger verification: the trigger verifies and atomically consumes the exact matching unconsumed authorization for the current transaction/binding, tenant, evidence record, and permitted operation/transition. Records for another transaction, backend/binding context, tenant, evidence record, operation, or invalid/expired verified context cannot match.
  • Single-use and no replay: atomic consumption (UPDATE ... WHERE consumed_at IS NULL RETURNING) permits at most one matching controlled update. A second update requires a new authorized procedure call and new authorization record; reused or already-consumed authorization fails closed.
  • Atomicity and rollback: authorization creation, evidence update, custody-event append, and authorization consumption must occur in the same database transaction. Commit makes all durable; rollback discards all effects, including inserted authorization rows, leaving no reusable authorization.
  • Nested SECURITY DEFINER execution: a SECURITY INVOKER caller of a SECURITY DEFINER function runs the function body with the owner's privileges, but the call still requires EXECUTE. Definer code must not be invokable without explicit privilege and must not expose security-internal records to unauthorized roles.
  • Ownership, EXECUTE grants, search_path, role separation: owners are NOLOGIN least-privilege roles (e.g. cares_security_owner and/or cares_evidence_owner) with no broader rights than required. All definer functions/procedures/triggers use fixed search_path = pg_catalog, security (and explicitly qualified application objects as needed), REVOKE ALL ... FROM PUBLIC, no unsafe dynamic SQL/unqualified object references, and explicit minimal EXECUTE grants only to narrowly authorized roles (never PUBLIC, cares_runtime, or cares_worker). Ordinary runtime, worker, ingest, reader, and administrative application roles cannot INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE security.evidence_transition_authorization, cannot directly UPDATE/DELETE forensic_evidence or evidence_custody_event, and cannot create/alter/own/grant these definer objects.
  • No generic bypass: no role may obtain a blanket evidence-mutation bypass flag; each authorization is narrowly scoped to one evidence row, one permitted operation/transition, and one current transaction/binding.

4.3 Custody-event append-only enforcement, sequencing, and hash chain

NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: evidence_custody_event is append-only and must define an explicit per-evidence sequence in addition to hash-chain linkage.

Illustrative schema additions/constraints:

-- illustrative additions to evidence_custody_event
custody_sequence bigint NOT NULL CHECK (custody_sequence > 0),
event_type text NOT NULL,
actor_id text NOT NULL,
occurred_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
request_or_job_id text,
object_hash_context bytea,
prior_event_hash bytea,
event_hash bytea,
UNIQUE (tenant_id, evidence_id, custody_sequence),
CHECK (
  (custody_sequence = 1 AND prior_event_hash IS NULL)
  OR (custody_sequence > 1 AND prior_event_hash IS NOT NULL)
)
  • Grant INSERT and SELECT only as required; revoke UPDATE and DELETE from PUBLIC, runtime, worker, and administrative application roles.
  • A trigger rejects UPDATE/DELETE on custody events.
  • Each event stores tenant_id, evidence_id, custody_sequence, event type, actor, timestamp, request/job, result, object hash/version context, prior_event_hash, and event_hash where hash chaining is used.

Hash-chain ordering/concurrency (illustrative append procedure, same transaction):

  1. Lock the evidence chain head deterministically, e.g. SELECT tenant_id, evidence_id FROM forensic_evidence WHERE tenant_id=:tenant AND evidence_id=:evidence FOR UPDATE (or a reviewed pg_advisory_xact_lock key derived from tenant/evidence when appropriate).
  2. Read the latest custody event for that (tenant_id, evidence_id) ordered by custody_sequence DESC and assign next_sequence = last_sequence + 1 (or 1 if none).
  3. Compute event_hash = H(canonical_event_fields || prior_event_hash) using the reviewed canonicalization.
  4. Insert exactly one next event with custody_sequence = next_sequence, prior_event_hash equal to the previous event hash (or NULL only for sequence 1), and the computed event_hash.
  5. Commit; concurrent inserters cannot obtain the same next sequence because of the chain-head lock and UNIQUE (tenant_id, evidence_id, custody_sequence).

For controlled evidence updates, authorization creation, the controlled forensic_evidence update, custody-event append, and authorization consumption must occur atomically in the same transaction. A failure at any step rolls back all effects, including any inserted authorization row, so no reusable authorization remains.

Verification:

  • recompute hashes in custody_sequence order from sequence 1 or a verified checkpoint;
  • verify no gaps/duplicates, each prior_event_hash link, canonical serialization, and required event sequence invariants;
  • compare stored evidence hash/version facts against the retrieved immutable object version when access/validation is performed.

Failure behavior:

  • set availability_state='integrity_failed' through controlled procedure only after recording a custody event describing the failure;
  • block merge/split, forensic export, and customer/legal delivery use of that evidence;
  • emit security alert/audit; require investigation and, if applicable, restore/revalidation.

4.4 Why a database hash chain is not independent tamper-proof storage

NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: A database hash chain detects accidental corruption and some unauthorized in-database modifications, but it is not equivalent to independent tamper-proof storage because:

  • a privileged database administrator, compromised definer function, migration, backup restore, or storage-layer attacker may alter rows and recompute a plausible chain;
  • the database, transaction logs, backups, and replicas are part of the same trust and operational domain unless separately protected;
  • chain integrity depends on canonicalization, key management (if signed), and correct verification tooling.

Independent controls, where approved, may include WORM/object-lock storage, externally stored signed manifests, separate audit ledgers, immutable backups, and restricted break-glass procedures. This document does not assume any of these are selected.

4.5 Controlled purge, restore, and reconciliation

  • Controlled purge: permitted only after retention eligibility, legal-hold clearance, reference checks, and required approvals. Record purge_requested and purged custody events, record tombstone/availability state, and preserve minimum metadata required by owner/legal policy. Never silently delete metadata or custody history.
  • Restore: restoring database rows or object versions must be followed by reconciliation that verifies object presence, version, hash, chain continuity, and references. Restored state is not automatically trusted until checks pass.
  • Reconciliation: periodic jobs compare registry metadata, custody chain, and storage objects. Missing objects, hash mismatches, version mismatches, or chain breaks produce integrity_failure records and alerts.
  • Compensation: merge/split corrections append new evidence references and operations; they never rewrite the original evidence object, hash, or historical custody chain.

NOT IMPLEMENTED / NOT TESTED: No evidence registry, storage integration, custody chain, purge workflow, or integrity verification exists.

5. Workstream D — RLS UPDATE and SELECT interaction

5.1 PostgreSQL behavior to account for

NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: PostgreSQL applies RLS according to command semantics, not by assuming that one permission implies another:

  • SELECT requires table/column privileges and applicable SELECT RLS policies.
  • INSERT uses INSERT privileges and INSERT WITH CHECK; INSERT ... RETURNING also requires SELECT visibility/privileges for returned columns/rows.
  • UPDATE uses UPDATE privileges and UPDATE USING to qualify existing rows and UPDATE WITH CHECK for resulting rows. Row qualification normally depends on reading existing rows/columns referenced by the statement, so SELECT privileges and SELECT RLS visibility are required for the rows/columns the command must read.
  • DELETE uses DELETE USING and normally also requires SELECT visibility for qualified rows.
  • RETURNING exposes row data and therefore requires SELECT access consistent with returned columns/rows.

The exact effective behavior must be validated on the selected PostgreSQL version and role/grant model. Do not assume UPDATE permission automatically provides SELECT visibility.

5.2 Asset read/write scope decision

NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: For CARES asset and identity tables, asset:write should imply asset:read for the same verified tenant and authorized row set.

Rationale:

  • Normal update flows need to locate, qualify, and often return the affected row.
  • Auditability and idempotency checks often require reading current state before mutation.
  • A “write-only but row-addressed update” is difficult to express safely under PostgreSQL RLS because row selection and RETURNING involve read semantics.

If a future use case requires blind writes, it must be designed explicitly (for example, append-only writes keyed by a pre-authorized identifier with no row qualification or returned data) and reviewed separately. This is not assumed for asset identity or licensing updates.

5.3 Illustrative policy alternatives

Alternative 1 — Recommended: write scope includes read scope

CREATE POLICY asset_select_scope
    ON asset
    AS RESTRICTIVE
    FOR SELECT
    TO cares_runtime, cares_worker
    USING (
        security.current_verified_scope_allows('asset:read')
        OR security.current_verified_scope_allows('asset:write')
    );

CREATE POLICY asset_insert_scope
    ON asset
    AS RESTRICTIVE
    FOR INSERT
    TO cares_runtime, cares_worker
    WITH CHECK (
        security.current_verified_scope_allows('asset:write')
    );

CREATE POLICY asset_update_scope
    ON asset
    AS RESTRICTIVE
    FOR UPDATE
    TO cares_runtime, cares_worker
    USING (security.current_verified_scope_allows('asset:write'))
    WITH CHECK (security.current_verified_scope_allows('asset:write'));

-- INSERT ... RETURNING and UPDATE ... RETURNING remain subject to SELECT policies.

Alternative 2 — Separate read and write scopes (stricter, operationally limited)

-- SELECT only with asset:read
USING (security.current_verified_scope_allows('asset:read'))

-- UPDATE only with asset:write
USING (security.current_verified_scope_allows('asset:write'))
WITH CHECK (security.current_verified_scope_allows('asset:write'))

This can block row-addressed updates or RETURNING unless the same assertion also carries asset:read. It may be appropriate for workflows where writes are rare and explicit dual-scope assertions are approved.

Alternative 3 — Blind append-only insert (special case only)

  • permit INSERT with asset:write;
  • do not permit RETURNING unless asset:read is present;
  • do not use row-addressed UPDATE ... WHERE against unreadable rows.

This is not suitable for canonical asset merge/split/licensing state transitions that require current-row visibility.

5.4 Command interaction matrix

Command pattern Required DB privileges RLS policies involved Expected result under recommended design
SELECT ... WHERE ... SELECT restrictive tenant floor + SELECT scope Allowed only for verified tenant and asset:read or asset:write
UPDATE ... WHERE ... UPDATE and effective SELECT on qualified/read columns tenant floor, UPDATE USING/WITH CHECK, and SELECT visibility for qualification Allowed only when write scope implies read and row passes update checks
UPDATE ... RETURNING ... UPDATE + SELECT on returned columns UPDATE policies and SELECT policies for returned rows/columns Allowed only with write-implied read (or explicit read scope)
INSERT ... VALUES ... INSERT tenant floor + INSERT WITH CHECK Allowed with write scope; tenant must match verified context
INSERT ... RETURNING ... INSERT + SELECT on returned columns INSERT WITH CHECK and SELECT visibility Requires read scope or write-implied read; otherwise no returned row
DELETE ... WHERE ... DELETE and effective SELECT tenant floor, DELETE USING, SELECT visibility Allowed only with delete scope and readable qualified rows
UPDATE changing tenant to another tenant UPDATE UPDATE USING and WITH CHECK Denied by restrictive WITH CHECK tenant floor

5.5 Acceptance tests

  1. SELECT with verified tenant and read scope succeeds; different tenant or missing context returns no rows/denies as applicable.
  2. UPDATE ... WHERE id = :id with write scope succeeds only for same-tenant readable row and fails for other-tenant row.
  3. UPDATE ... WHERE referencing columns not readable under SELECT policy fails or is denied; do not rely on implicit visibility.
  4. UPDATE ... RETURNING with write-only scope under Alternative 2 is denied/unreadable for returned data; under Alternative 1 it succeeds.
  5. INSERT ... RETURNING requires effective SELECT visibility for returned columns.
  6. UPDATE that attempts to set tenant_id to a different tenant fails WITH CHECK.
  7. Write scope for tenant A cannot update tenant B even if a forged or stale GUC names tenant B.
  8. Verify behavior on the selected PostgreSQL version for direct table access, updatable views (if any), and partitioned tables.

NOT TESTED: No PostgreSQL RLS command-interaction tests exist.

The following artifacts are illustrative only:

  • Workstream B: revised identity_operation_outbox, identity_operation_outbox_attempt, identity_operation_outbox_replay, claim/request-start/acknowledge pseudocode, expired-lease reclaimer pseudocode, and replay-apply pseudocode.
