7. Threat and failure scenarios

Area Scenario Required outcome
Context Forged SET cares.tenant_id Ignored by authorization helpers; no protected context row means deny
Context Valid assertion replayed after commit Nonce uniqueness rejects; no second protected write
Context Assertion retried after known rollback Allowed only within lifetime/policy and with business idempotency; nonce/context not previously committed
Context Pooled connection reused with stale session state Reset/discard required; stale GUC cannot authorize
Definer Unsafe search_path or unqualified object in definer function Rejected in review/tests; hardened function required
Outbox Worker lease expires before request starts Reclaim to retry/dead-letter based on policy; mark lease_expired_before_request
Outbox Worker lease expires after request starts, idempotent provider Fence token, preserve same idempotency ref, retry or reconcile
Outbox Worker lease expires after request starts, non-idempotent/unknown delivery_unknown, reconcile, no blind duplicate send
Outbox Two manual replay requests submitted concurrently Only one approved replay application for the target generation commits
Outbox Ack transaction fails after provider success Delivery may have happened; reconcile/retry idempotently or enter delivery_unknown
Evidence Direct update to immutable hash/object fields Trigger/procedure rejects
Evidence Custody event update/delete attempted Append-only enforcement rejects
Evidence Hash-chain verification fails Record failure, set integrity failed, block forensic/merge use, alert
Evidence DB row hash chain looks valid but external storage tampered independently Object hash/version verification must still detect mismatch; DB chain alone is insufficient
Evidence Restore brings back metadata without object Reconciliation marks unavailable/integrity issue; do not claim evidence usable
RLS UPDATE ... RETURNING with insufficient read visibility Denied/not returned according to PostgreSQL behavior and policy design
RLS Write scope lacks read scope in row-addressed workflow Operation fails; use approved write-implies-read or dual-scope design
RLS INSERT ... RETURNING without read visibility Insert may be allowed by policy but returned data must not leak; design must be explicit and tested

8. State-transition details

8.1 Verified context lifecycle (conceptual)

State Entry condition Exit condition
Unverified Transaction started, no protected context row Successful verifier bind or transaction end
Verified/bound Verifier inserted nonce and current-transaction context row Commit, rollback, or expiry/invalidation handling
Consumed-for-commit Transaction commits with nonce/context effects New transaction requires new assertion
Discarded Rollback clears uncommitted nonce/context effects Assertion may be retried only if still valid and policy allows

8.2 Outbox lifecycle

Key states: pending, leased, retry_wait, delivered, delivery_unknown, dead_letter, cancelled.

Critical transitions are defined in Workstream B and must preserve: fenced lease tokens, append-only attempts, monotonic cumulative attempt count, replay-generation authorization, and no blind resend when non-idempotent delivery is ambiguous.

8.3 Evidence availability lifecycle

State Meaning Allowed transitions
available Registered object/hash/custody valid for controlled use purge_pending, integrity_failed
purge_pending Approved purge workflow in progress purged, available (approved cancellation)
purged Object payload disposition completed per approved policy; tombstone/metadata retained as required none, except audited metadata correction prohibition still applies
integrity_failed Hash/version/chain/reconciliation failure available only after controlled revalidation or restoration and custody event

Original evidence object/hash metadata is never rewritten in place to “fix” history.

9. Acceptance tests

All tests below are required before claiming implementation readiness; they are NOT TESTED now.

A. Trusted context and GUC forgery

  1. Set forged tenant GUC and run SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE without a valid protected context record: deny.
  2. Set forged tenant GUC after valid context bind: verified tenant/scope remain unchanged.
  3. Attempt direct DML on security.tenant_context_nonce and security.verified_transaction_context as runtime roles: deny.
  4. Replay committed assertion in a new transaction: nonce conflict/deny.
  5. Roll back after verifier bind and retry same valid assertion: allowed by protocol; committed effects not duplicated.
  6. Simulate unknown commit and retry with fresh assertion plus same business idempotency key: single logical outcome.
  7. Reuse pooled connection/session: stale GUC cannot authorize; missing reset forces discard.
  8. Validate every SECURITY DEFINER function has fixed search_path, restricted execute grants, no unsafe dynamic SQL, and cannot be shadowed; verify narrow helpers do not expose the full verified context record.
  9. Verify committed verified-context cleanup/removal cannot affect an active backend/transaction/binding and that backend PID or transaction-identifier reuse cannot authorize a later transaction.
  10. Directly call verifier, clear, cleanup, and context helper functions as unauthorized roles: deny or no sensitive result.

B. Outbox reclaimer and replay

  1. Lease expires with provider_request_phase='not_started': reclaimer marks lease_expired_before_request and moves to retry/dead-letter per policy.
  2. Lease expires after request_started with idempotent provider: same provider idempotency reference preserved; retry/reconcile path allowed.
  3. Lease expires after request_started without safe idempotency: moves to delivery_unknown.
  4. Stale worker attempts acknowledgement after reclaimer fences token: update affects zero rows.
  5. Reclaimer and stale worker race: exactly one terminal handling of that attempt.
  6. Two concurrent manual replay apply requests for same target generation: exactly one applied.
  7. Duplicate replay request after applied generation: returns existing state; no new external side effect.
  8. attempt_count remains cumulative/monotonic, generation_attempt_count enforces per-generation max_attempts, and attempt_number/generation_attempt_number/replay_generation remain consistent across claim, expiry, retry, and replay.
  9. delivery_unknown cannot transition to retry_wait without explicit reconciliation evidence and required authorization; ambiguous/non-idempotent replay requires enforced duplicate_risk_accepted.
  10. Authorized replay after per-generation limit increments replay_generation, resets only generation_attempt_count, preserves cumulative attempt_count, and retains the original provider idempotency reference unless a separately approved new logical side effect is recorded.

C. Evidence immutability and custody

  1. Direct UPDATE of every immutable forensic_evidence field (including nullable fields via IS DISTINCT FROM enforcement) fails.
  2. Direct DELETE of forensic_evidence and evidence_custody_event fails for runtime, worker, and administrative application roles.
  3. Runtime role manually setting the old GUC to on (for example SET security.evidence_controlled_transition = 'on' or set_config('security.evidence_controlled_transition','on',true)) cannot authorize a controlled evidence-field update; authorization decisions do not read GUCs.
  4. Runtime role attempting direct UPDATE of controlled evidence fields (retention_policy_id, legal_hold, availability_state) fails without an exact protected transaction-bound authorization.
  5. Runtime role attempting to create a fake authorization record in security.evidence_transition_authorization fails with permission denied (security-internal table, no runtime/worker/admin application DML privileges).
  6. Authorization for evidence A cannot be used to update evidence B (exact tenant_id/evidence_id match required); authorization for tenant A cannot be used against tenant B.
  7. Reusing an authorization record for a second controlled update in the same or a later transaction fails because the authorization is consumed atomically on the first successful matching update and is not reusable.
  8. If the transaction rolls back after authorization creation and/or evidence update, no reusable authorization remains and a later attempt cannot reuse the rolled-back authorization.
  9. Unauthorized direct invocation of controlled procedures fails (missing/invalid verified context, missing scope, insufficient EXECUTE privilege, or failed transition authorization/preconditions).
  10. A successful authorized transition performs exactly one controlled evidence update and appends exactly one custody event atomically with authorization creation/consumption in the same transaction.
  11. Concurrent attempts to reuse or satisfy the same authorization cannot both succeed: at most one update consumes the unconsumed matching authorization row; the other fails closed.
  12. Legal-hold, retention-metadata, and availability transitions succeed only through approved controlled procedures with protected transaction-bound authorization, custody events, and enforced allowed transitions; disallowed transitions fail with no partial state change.
  13. Concurrent custody-event inserts for the same evidence produce unique custody_sequence values, no gaps/duplicates/missing links, and a verifiable hash chain.
  14. Hash-chain verification failure sets integrity_failed through controlled procedure, blocks protected uses, appends an auditable custody event, and emits alert/audit.
  15. Object hash mismatch with valid-looking DB metadata is detected at access/verification time.
  16. Purge workflow enforces legal hold/reference/approval checks and leaves required tombstone/custody records.
  17. Restore/reconciliation detects missing object, version mismatch, or broken chain and does not silently accept evidence.

D. RLS UPDATE/SELECT interaction

  1. SELECT allowed/denied by verified tenant and read-or-write-implied scope as designed.
  2. UPDATE ... WHERE requires effective read visibility of qualified rows/columns.
  3. UPDATE ... RETURNING requires SELECT visibility for returned data.
  4. INSERT ... RETURNING requires SELECT visibility for returned data.
  5. Write-only scope without read implication cannot read/return rows; behavior matches selected design and is documented.
  6. Cross-tenant UPDATE/RETURNING attempts fail.
  7. Policy alternatives are tested on the selected PostgreSQL version, including partitions and any approved views.

10. Remaining owner/security decisions

The following remain OWNER DECISION REQUIRED or require explicit security-owner approval:

  1. PostgreSQL major/minor version and whether required transaction-binding features, security_invoker views, and cryptographic verification options are available and approved.
  2. Assertion signature algorithm, verifier implementation, key custody, rotation, revocation, TTL, clock-skew allowance, nonce retention, and emergency response.
  3. Whether HMAC shared-secret trust is acceptable if asymmetric verification is not selected; HMAC database compromise implications must be formally accepted.
  4. Exact transaction-binding mechanism for verified context records and whether any non-GUC handle/reference is permitted for observability only.
  5. Runtime, worker, verifier, reclaimer, ingest, reader, maintenance, and break-glass role model, including grants, BYPASSRLS, and SECURITY DEFINER ownership.
  6. Provider-specific idempotency, receipt/lookup capabilities, retention of idempotency keys, reconciliation workflow, and conditions for manual replay of ambiguous/non-idempotent effects.
  7. Evidence retention, legal hold, customer deletion, tombstone/hash retention, backup purge/reconciliation, and object-lock/WORM expectations.
  8. Approved evidence object storage, tenant isolation model, access path, versioning guarantees, and independent tamper-evidence controls if required.
  9. Whether asset:write implies asset:read globally for affected CARES tables or only for specific workflows/tables.
  10. Operational ownership for outbox dead-letter handling, integrity-failure response, and evidence restore/reconciliation.

13. Final Technical Corrections and Remaining Decisions

Corrections made

  • Trusted transaction context privilege chain and cleanup: clarified nested execution (a SECURITY INVOKER caller of a SECURITY DEFINER function runs the definer body with owner privileges, but still requires EXECUTE). Replaced full-record context exposure with narrowly scoped definer helpers (context_is_valid, current_verified_tenant_id, current_verified_scope_allows) that return only boolean/UUID decisions, plus verifier/clear/maintenance function boundaries. Defined illustrative ownership (NOLOGIN security/evidence owners), REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC, fixed search_path, role-specific EXECUTE grants, and no direct runtime/worker access to nonce/context tables. Added explicit cleanup/binding requirements (binding_epoch or equivalent), current-transaction-only matching, backend PID/transaction identifier reuse handling, abandoned-connection and pool-reuse behavior, and fail-closed rules.
  • Evidence immutability completeness and null safety: enumerated every immutable forensic_evidence field (including nullable fields), separated immutable fields from controlled fields (retention_policy_id, legal_hold, availability_state), and aligned the illustrative trigger with that inventory using PostgreSQL IS DISTINCT FROM for nullable comparisons. Specified controlled procedures for legal hold, retention metadata, and availability transitions; prohibited direct UPDATE/DELETE for ordinary runtime, worker, and administrative application roles. Added per-evidence custody custody_sequence with UNIQUE (tenant_id, evidence_id, custody_sequence), append-only constraints, and a lock/read-next-sequence/hash/insert protocol to prevent duplicate sequence numbers, missing links, or ambiguous ordering under concurrency.
  • Outbox attempt limits and ambiguous replay: defined max_attempts as a per-replay-generation limit enforced via explicit generation_attempt_count, while keeping attempt_count cumulative and monotonic and attempt_number as the unique cumulative attempt row identifier. Added generation_attempt_number for per-generation auditability, reset only generation_attempt_count on authorized replay application, and preserved authorized replay after a generation limit is reached. Required delivery_unknown -> retry_wait transitions to have explicit reconciliation evidence, provider outcome, and required authorization; enforced duplicate_risk_accepted where ambiguous/non-idempotent duplicate risk remains. Preserved original request_idempotency_key/provider_idempotency_ref unless a separately approved new logical side effect is explicitly created.
  • DDL/consistency corrections: corrected payload jsonb jsonb NOT NULL to payload jsonb NOT NULL, added missing outbox/replay/custody fields and constraints needed by the corrected protocols, and aligned claim/reclaimer/replay/state-transition text with the schema. All SQL and pseudocode remain illustrative, not production-ready migrations.

Issues that remain unresolved

  • NOT IMPLEMENTED / NOT TESTED: no PostgreSQL schema, migrations, roles, RLS policies, verifier/context functions, nonce/context storage, outbox workers/reclaimers, evidence registry, custody procedures, or production-equivalent verification tests exist.
  • The exact PostgreSQL transaction/binding mechanism (transaction_ref, binding_epoch, current-transaction/binding helpers) must be selected and validated for the approved PostgreSQL version; this document does not assume a specific function, extension, or lifecycle guarantee.
  • Provider-specific reconciliation APIs, receipt formats, idempotency retention windows, and ambiguous-delivery handling remain integration-specific and unverified.
  • Evidence object-store behavior, legal/retention controls, restore reconciliation, and independent tamper-evidence controls remain unselected and unverified.
  • Controlled-transition enforcement for evidence procedures (including any transaction-local guard mechanism) must be reviewed so it cannot become an authorization bypass.

Owner/security decisions still required

  • PostgreSQL major/minor version and approved transaction/binding, cryptographic, and view/RLS features.
  • Assertion signature algorithm, verifier implementation, key custody/rotation/revocation, TTL, clock skew, nonce retention, and emergency response.
  • Final role/grant model and ownership for verifier, context helpers, cleanup, evidence procedures, outbox/replay operations, maintenance, and break-glass access.
  • Provider-specific idempotency, reconciliation evidence standards, retry/backoff/dead-letter ownership, and authorization for ambiguous/non-idempotent replay including when duplicate_risk_accepted may be approved.
  • Evidence storage/versioning, retention, legal hold, customer deletion, tombstone/hash retention, backup purge/reconciliation, and independent tamper-evidence controls.
  • Confirmation of whether asset:write implies asset:read for all approved CARES row-addressed workflows/tables.

Readiness for formal PostgreSQL schema/security review

  • Ready for formal PostgreSQL schema/security review: yes, for the corrected trusted-context, outbox recovery/replay, evidence immutability/custody, and RLS UPDATE/SELECT interaction areas, subject to the unresolved decisions above.
  • Not ready for production migration or implementation: no approved PostgreSQL binding/verifier implementation, no migrations, no runtime roles/policies/functions, no workers/reclaimers, no evidence storage integration, and no production-equivalent tests.
